newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Mandela sees negotiated end to Zaire civil war.
newsitem.headline: Mandela sees negotiated end to Zaire civil war.

text.p: South African President Nelson Mandela said on Thursday that after talks with Zaire rebel leader Laurent Kabila and President Mobutu Sese Seko he was confident of a peaceful end to Zaire's civil war.

"I have been speaking both to (rebel) president (Laurent) Kabila and to (Zairean) President Mobutu, and as a result of the exchanges I have had with them, and the other leaders in Africa, I am confident that a peaceful solution will be achieved," Mandela told reporters.
African elder statesman Mandela, who held an hour-long session on Wednesday evening with Kabila, said he had also spoken to Mobutu three times since last Saturday.

"He (Kabila), doesn't want a military solution. He has made this clear over and over again. He wants a solution which will receive the support of President Mobutu and he has also made it clear that he has no intention of doing anything which will humiliate President Mobutu," the South African president said.
Of Mobutu he said:"He is very cooperative, but what he is going to do eventually, I cannot predict."
"I believe he himself has an interest in a negotiated settlement."

Mandela's spokesman Joel Netshitenzhe told Reuters the talks with Kabila in Cape Town on Wednesday night explored possible new initiatives to end the fighting between Kabila's rebel force and Mobutu's troops.

Kabila, whose forces hold about half Zaire, on Thursday left Cape Town in a South African Air Force plane which was flying him back to Lubumbashi, Zaire's second city, which his forces seized last week.
Kabila could soon meet the man he is trying to topple, sources close to the talks said. Representatives of Mobutu were in Cape Town but it was not clear if they met Kabila, the sources said.
In the capital Kinshasa, Zairean Information Minister Kin-Kiey Mulumba told a Wednesday news conference Mobutu and Kabila could meet directly once their envoys had consulted.
"Things are getting clearer. Plans are afoot for a meeting between the head of state and the rebel leader. This meeting is imminent," Kin-Kiey said.
A senior South African source said Mandela wanted to bring Mobutu and Kabila together in South Africa as part of his peace brokering.

Deputy Foreign Affairs Minister Aziz Pahad was instrumental in arranging earlier talks in South Africa between representatives of the Zairean rivals and was expected to be involved in any new arrangements.
Speaking to reporters on Wednesday, Kabila took a hard line:" There will be no ceasefire until Mobutu relinquishes power," he said.
Kabila, head of the Alliance of Democratic Forces for the Liberation of Congo-Zaire, had earlier told Reuters by telephone the "people are against a ceasefire".
"The people do not want a ceasefire, they want an end to this corrupt regime," said Kabila. That heightened fear of a tragedy in Kinshasa should rebel forces reach the capital.

Kabila's rebels say they are 300 km (180 miles) from Kinshasa, a claim ridiculed by the government. But given the inability of Zaire's undisciplined army to offer resistance, many Zaireans doubt government forces can hold Kinshasa.
